## What you build {#build}

An autonomous system with a complete **sense → propose → permit → act → observe → revise** loop. A learned policy proposes a move. An independent microcontroller decides whether to permit it. The arm changes the world, and a fresh observation informs the next decision.

The proposed station combines a Seeed SO-101 arm, an overhead camera, and an Arduino UNO Q. Its Linux processor runs the policy; its STM32 microcontroller governs the motor command path. Staff qualify the station and provide the baseline firmware before student use.

::: {.eth-loop}
![Camera observations feed a Linux policy; proposals cross an authority boundary to the STM32 governor, which permits bounded motor commands. Measured motion and a new camera image close the loop.](../../assets/images/vol4-control-loop.svg)

[Open the control-loop diagram](../../assets/images/vol4-control-loop.svg)
:::

The final deliverable is a **Physical Release Dossier**: the operating envelope, baseline comparisons, raw traces, failure evidence, and a defended release decision. A rigorous decision to withhold release can earn full marks. The [competency card](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol4/curriculum/student-competencies.html) defines the skills demonstrated along the way.

## A semester at the bench {#studio}

The provisional weekly rhythm pairs a systems seminar with a supervised hardware studio. Read the assigned chapter before seminar, bring a prediction to the bench, and record what the physical system actually did. Teams maintain one shared notebook that accumulates evidence across the semester.

```{=html}
<div class="eth-phases">
  <section><span>01 · WEEKS 1–4</span><h3>Measure the machine.</h3><p>Establish physical limits, derive kinematics, and compare the digital twin with the real arm.</p></section>
  <section><span>02 · WEEKS 5–9</span><h3>Teach it to act.</h3><p>Evaluate a learned policy, collect demonstrations, adapt it, and test recovery when the world changes.</p></section>
  <section><span>03 · WEEKS 10–14</span><h3>Defend its behavior.</h3><p>Build the governor, inject declared faults, and defend a bounded release decision for your capstone.</p></section>
</div>
```

The [syllabus](syllabus.qmd#schedule) is the canonical source for weekly readings, checkpoints, assessment, and policies. Meeting times, rooms, credits, and enrollment details will be confirmed by course staff.

## The tools and what they do {#tools}

The stack serves the experiment. Staff pin the tested versions and supply starter assets; the reference station determines which policy and export path become required.

- **LeRobot + PyTorch:** demonstration datasets, training, and policy evaluation. Training runs on workstation compute; deployment is evaluated on the edge station.
- **ACT and SmolVLA:** candidate learned policies. ACT provides action chunking from images and robot state; SmolVLA adds language conditioning. Their station performance must be qualified.
- **MuJoCo or PyBullet:** the simulator choice remains to be pinned by staff. The twin models the same arm and supports matched simulation and hardware trials.
- **OpenCV + V4L2:** camera calibration, acquisition, and configuration.
- **ONNX Runtime / INT8:** the proposed edge deployment path, subject to export, numerical parity, memory, and timing checks.
- **STM32 C + the qualified Arduino/STM32 toolchain:** deterministic command permission, bounds, and watchdog behavior.

The [station reference](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol4/labs/station-reference.html) defines the hardware, wiring, and four action taps. Isaac Sim and Cosmos are potential research extensions; their use would depend on a staff-qualified experiment.

## Before week one {#prepare}

Bring working Python skills, introductory ML intuition, basic linear algebra and probability, and first-year Newtonian physics. Prior robot-arm or microcontroller experience is helpful; staff provide the baseline firmware and support its extension.

1. Read the Volume IV [reader guide](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol4/frontmatter/prerequisites.html) and [The Causal Boundary](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol4/01_boundary/01_boundary.html).
2. Review the [course syllabus](syllabus.qmd), including the assessment and team-work expectations.
3. Follow the [Getting Started lab](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol4/labs/week-01-getting-started.html) when the teaching team releases the qualified station instructions.

::: {.eth-closing}
**The course's governing question:** What must the system measure, constrain, and demonstrate before a learned proposal becomes a physical action?
:::
